title: Add human-friendly release titles and sampled onboard metadata preview
author: Elena Park
description:
Motivation: Model release notes and onboarding artifacts are machine-accurate but often hard for humans to scan quickly. For consumers (platform engineers, product managers, and release notes), a succinct, human-friendly release title and a small sampled metadata preview help triage relevance and expedite reviews.

What this PR does: Implements a lightweight 'release title generator' that synthesizes a short human-readable title from model onboard metadata (tags, performance tokens, stability notes, major changes). Adds a sampled-metadata previewer CLI that selects representative fields and example inference stats to include in changelogs and release note headings. All behavior is opt-in for onboarders and defaults to a conservative title heuristic to avoid misleading summaries.

Design notes: Title generator is a heuristic with rules prioritized to preserve factual accuracy: 1) prefer explicit release_label metadata if present; 2) otherwise combine dominant-affordance (e.g., 'chat', 'completion', 'embedding') + biggest perf delta (e.g., latency/cost/quality) + a short scope token (e.g., 'smaller-vocab', 'sparse-kv'). Titles are limited to 8 words. The sampler walks available telemetry (sampled latencies, token-distribution percentiles) and picks up to three representative lines for the release preview. Implementation keeps generation deterministic given the same seed.

Why this is safe: No metadata is created or overwritten on existing models; the generator only suggests a title and preview bundle. The CLI writes suggestions to a local file or to a draft release object when the user passes --write-draft. All telemetry reads use the existing read-only export APIs and respect onboard privacy flags.

Compatibility: Works with current onboard manifest schema v2 and falls back gracefully for v1 manifests (title components will be inferred only from available fields). The CLI is added under /cli and is discoverable via docs.

Checklist:
- [x] Title generator library (src/onboard/title_generator.py)
- [x] Command-line preview tool (cli/release_title_preview.py)
- [x] Unit tests for heuristics and deterministic seeding (tests/test_title_gen.py)
- [x] Documentation page and quickstart (docs/model-onboard/release-title-guidelines.md)
- [x] Integration test to ensure no manifest writes without explicit flag (tests/test_cli_no_write.py)
- [x] Add Linear link in PR (ENG-6682)

Risks and mitigations: The biggest risk is a low-quality automated title that misrepresents changes. Mitigation: titles are suggestions only and are visible as drafts until a human accepts them. Added a short guidance copy in docs to avoid over-reliance.

How to exercise locally: python cli/release_title_preview.py --manifest examples/manifests/sample-v2.json --seed 42 --format markdown

Expected follow-ups: 1) telemetry to measure acceptance rate of suggested titles (ENG-6720), 2) a short UX tweak to surface titles in the console release UI (PM-421).

review_comments: Ravi Patel: Nice ergonomics. One question — how do we prevent the generator from producing wording that implies breaking API changes? Suggest adding a blacklist of 'breaking' verbs.
Author (Elena Park): Good call. I've added a conservative blacklist and a final 'safety' pass that strips candidate verbs that match our breaking_verb_list (see title_generator.py).
Jinsoo Kim: Tests look good; should we add a small end-to-end that runs the CLI against a telemetry export? It can be opt-in in CI.

Author (Elena Park): I added tests/test_cli_no_write.py to assert no writes without --write-draft and added a small sample manifest to examples/; opted not to add a full telemetry CI step in this PR to keep CI time bounded.

release_notes:
- Add suggested human-friendly release titles for model onboard drafts.
- Add a sampled metadata preview CLI to surface representative telemetry and manifest fields for release notes.
- Documentation and tests included.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on the title heuristics and the blacklist safety pass. The code is intentionally conservative; hard rules are in title_generator.py and unit coverage is provided. If we want additional signals (example prompts / eval-based snippets) that can be a follow-up change.
